tool.description: Run Office.js JavaScript inside an already-provided host wrapper. Excel uses async function runOfficeJsScript(ctx, Excel, console) { ... }; PowerPoint uses async function runOfficeJsScript(ctx, PowerPoint, console) { ... }. In PowerPoint scripts, use readPowerPointAttachmentPptxBase64(fileId) to stage an attached PPTX source for native template-slide import, then pass that value directly into insertSlidesFromBase64(..., { formatting: "KeepSourceFormatting" }) without inspecting, logging, or returning it. Use this when it is the fastest accurate path for host-native work that exceeds the direct primitive tools. Keep scripts scoped to the intended workbook, presentation, slides, shapes, or charts. Provide only the function body; top-level return is surfaced.
tool.name: run_officejs

summary.description: Short label shown next to the tool icon. 4-8 words describing in active tense what is happening

extended_summary.description: Extended summary of what is happening. 10-12 words describing in active tense what is happening. Use this to explain the script in more detail.

code.description: Function body only for the active host wrapper. Excel exposes (ctx, Excel, console); PowerPoint exposes (ctx, PowerPoint, console).

destructive.description: Optional legacy metadata for UI summaries. You may omit it; if included, set true when the script edits the active Office document.

references.description: Optional user-visible references for the touched target. Excel may use A1 ranges such as ['Sheet1!A1:C10']; PowerPoint may omit this or use concise slide/object labels when useful.
